The '''Certificate Management Protocol''' (CMP) is an Internet protocol standardized by the [[Internet Engineering Task Force|IETF]] used for obtaining X.509 [[Public key certificate|public-key certificates]] in a [[public key infrastructure|PKI]].

CMP is a very feature-rich and flexible protocol.
So far it is the only protocol with support of all types of cryptography. This includes KEM keys, which have become more important for [[post-quantum_cryptography|post-quantum cryptography (PQC)]].

CMP messages are self-contained, which makes the protocol independent of the transport mechanism and provides end-to-end security also over multiple hops. This distinguishes CMP and [[Certificate Management over CMS|CMC]] from other certificate enrollment protocols including [[Enrollment over Secure Transport|EST]].
CMP messages are defined in [[ASN.1]] syntax and encoded using the [[Distinguished Encoding Rules|DER]] method.

CMP is described in {{IETF RFC|9810}}. Enrollment request messages employ the Certificate Request Message Format (CRMF), described in {{IETF RFC|4211}} and updated in {{IETF RFC|9045}}.
The only other protocol so far using CRMF is [[Certificate Management over CMS]] (CMC), described in {{IETF RFC|5273}}.

== History ==
The initial version of CMP is described in {{IETF RFC|2510}}, the respective CRMF version in {{IETF RFC|2511}}. Both were published in March 1999.

CMP version 2 was described in {{IETF RFC|4210}}, published in September 2005. HTTP transfer for CMP messages was first described by {{IETF RFC|6712}}, published in September 2012.

In November 2023, [https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9480 CMP Updates], [https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9481 CMP Algorithms], and [https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9482 CoAP transfer for CMP], have been published as well as the [https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9483 Lightweight CMP Profile] focusing on industrial use.

In July 2025, [https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9810.html RFC 9810] was released, which combines the RFCs 4210 and 9480 into a self-contained document and adds further features, in particular support for [[Key_encapsulation_mechanism|KEM]] keys. At the same time, an update of the specification for HTTP(S) transfer of CMP messages was published in [https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9811.html RFC 9811].

== PKI Entities ==
In a [[public key infrastructure|Public-Key Infrastructure]] (PKI), so-called '''end entities''' (EEs) act as CMP client, requesting one or more certificates for themselves from a [[certificate authority]] (CA), which issues the legal certificates and acts as a CMP server. None or any number of [[registration authority|registration authorities]] (RA), can be used to mediate between the EEs and CAs, having both a downstream CMP server interface and an upstream CMP client interface. Using a "cross-certification request" a CA can get a certificate signed by another CA.

== Features ==
* Self-contained messages with protection being independent of message transfer – as opposed to related protocols [[Enrollment over Secure Transport|EST]] and [[Simple Certificate Enrollment Protocol|SCEP]], this supports built-in end-to-end proof of origin also over several hops.
* Proof of possession (POP) is usually done by a self-signature of the requested certificate contents, but CMP supports also other methods. This is crucial in particular for requesting certificates for [[Key_encapsulation_mechanism|KEM]]-only keys.
* CMP supports the very important aspect of proof of origin (i.e., proof of identity of the requester) in two variants: MAC-based with a shared secret (used initially) and signature-based (using pre-existing certificates).
* Key pair generation is usually done by the client side, but can also be requested from the server side.
* In case an end entity has lost its private key and it is stored by the CA, it might be recovered by requesting a "key pair recovery".
* Full certificate life-cycle support: an end entity can utilize CMP to obtain certificates from a CA, request updates for them, and also get them revoked.
* There are various further types of requests possible, for instance to retrieve CA certificates and to obtain PKI parameters and preferences of the server side.

== Transport ==
CMP messages are usually transferred over HTTP(S), but any reliable means of transportation can be used.
* Encapsulated in [[Hypertext Transfer Protocol|HTTP]] messages,<ref>[http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc9811 RFC 9811 (formerly: RFC 6712) Internet X.509 Public Key Infrastructure – HTTP Transfer for the Certificate Management Protocol (CMP)]</ref> optionally using TLS ([[Hypertext Transfer Protocol Secure|HTTPS]]) for additional protection.
* Encapsulated in [[Constrained Application Protocol|CoAP]] messages, optionally using [[Datagram Transport Layer Security|DTLS]] for additional protection.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9482 | title=Constrained Application Protocol (CoAP) Transfer for the Certificate Management Protocol | date=November 2023 | last1=Sahni | first1=Mohit | last2=Tripathi | first2=Saurabh }}</ref>
* [[Transmission Control Protocol|TCP]] or any other reliable, connection-oriented transport protocol.
* As a [[Computer file|file]], e.g., over [[File Transfer Protocol|FTP]] or [[Secure Copy|SCP]].
* By [[email]], using the [[Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions|MIME]] encoding standard.

The [[Content-Type]] used is ''application/pkixcmp''. Initially, ''application/pkixcmp-poll'', ''application/x-pkixcmp'' or ''application/x-pkixcmp-poll'' were used.

== Implementations ==
{{Refexample|section|date=October 2021}}
* [[OpenSSL]] since version 3.0 includes extensive CMP support in C.<br> The so-called [https://github.com/siemens/gencmpclient generic CMP client] provides a high-level API for it, adhering to the [https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9483.html Lightweight CMP Profile] defined in {{IETF RFC|9483}}.
* [[Bouncy Castle (cryptography)|Bouncy Castle]] offers CMP support in Java and C#.<ref name="ejbca" />
* [[RSA BSAFE#Cert-J|RSA BSAFE Cert-J]] provides CMP support in C and Java.
* [[cryptlib]] provides CMP support in C.
* The [[certificate authority|CA]] software products [[EJBCA]]<ref name="ejbca">{{Cite web |url=https://www.ejbca.org/news/tech-update-ejbca-cmp/ |title=Tech update – CMP in EJBCA and Bouncy Castle |access-date=2022-06-21}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://ejbca.org/features.html |title=EJBCA - The Java EE Certificate Authority |access-date=2019-06-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190607065910/https://ejbca.org/features.html |archive-date=2019-06-07 |url-status=dead }}</ref>, Insta Certifier, Entrust Certificate Authority, Nexus Certificate Manager, DigiCert Device Trust Manager, and IBM z/OS PKI Services, implement subsets of CMPv2.
